subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or documented current backup limits?
rationale: Choosing default exclusions, protected backup contents, and progress/size behavior affects restore completeness and sensitive-state handling, so automation should not settle the policy while an open linked PR is under review.

options.title: Review linked native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving proof, compatibility, protected-path semantics, and restore-safety concerns.

options.title: Ship minimal reliability first
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with progress or size guidance while deferring smart/custom exclusions to the broader native exclude-pattern tracker.

options.title: Document core limits
options.body: Declare that current coarse backup scopes are the intended core boundary and point optional backup strategies to plugin or ClawHub paths only after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review linked native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving proof, compatibility, protected-path semantics, and restore-safety concerns.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest history signal for the backup archive ownership boundary and original backup CLI contract.
